key_entities: untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge
propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired files non-atomically without rollback, leaving the working tree dirty when the detached sweep process is interrupted or killed.

When reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets, it fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge' if a peer clone pushed the same *.retired/SNAPSHOT paths to origin, causing a permanent wedge.
The current abort-only merge failure handler and push-recovery (git reset --hard tracked-only, stash without -u) cannot clear untracked files, causing every retry to re-abort identically.
Local ticket events and commits become stranded off origin when the store wedges, unreachable if the worktree is removed.

Relocating named untracked paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree and retrying the merge once will self-heal the untracked-collision case while preserving both parents and all local commits.

Tracked .archived files committed to HEAD before gitignore rules were added remain dirty (worktree deletions) even after recovery, causing plan-review and completion attestation operations to fail on git status checks.
